title: Principality of Bulgaria
capsule: The Principality of Bulgaria was an autonomous vassal state under nominal Ottoman suzerainty, created by the Treaty of Berlin (July 1878) after Russia's victory in the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–78. Its first ruler, Alexander I of Battenberg, presided over the unification with Eastern Rumelia in 1885, defying both the Great Powers and the Ottoman Porte. Ferdinand I proclaimed full independence in 1908, transforming the principality into the Tsardom of Bulgaria; Bulgaria then fought in the Balkan Wars and both World Wars, ending with the abolition of the monarchy in September 1946.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is well documented through Ottoman and Austro-Hungarian diplomatic records, treaty maps, and Bulgarian state archives, though exact borders shifted significantly after the 1885 unification and Balkan Wars.
